Table 2: Site-level benefit-cost analysis
                       Uganda             Philippines        Bangladesh
                       Individual Group   Individual Group   Individual Group  Ind. Light
Panel A: Estimated Program Costs
Cost per household at year 1                 $9,079  $8,099  $1,901 $1,392 $3,531 $2,866 $2,486
Cost per household discounted (5% per year)  $10,060 $8,974  $2,107 $1,543 $5,014 $4,070 $3,530
Panel B: Estimated Program Benefits
Monthly consumption per adult equiv  $27 [$22,$32]  $30 [$24,$36]  $18 [$6,$30]  $19 [$8,$29]  $20 [$10,$30]  $15 [$7,$23]  $10 [$2,$17]
Annual total household consumption   $1,348 [$1,080,$1,616] $1,512 ... $291 [$52,$530]
Total benefits at persistence of ... 100% $24,336 $27,284 $15,544 $15,948 $11,199 $8,315 $5,254
                                      90% $7,553 ...   80% $4,056 ...
Panel C: Cost Benefit Ratios
Benefit-cost ratio at persistence of ... 100% 2.9 [2.3,3.4] 3.6 [2.9,4.3] 7.4 [2.5,12.4] 10.4 [4.7,16.1] 3.1 [1.6,4.6] 2.8 [1.3,4.3] 2.1 [0.4,3.7]
                                          90% 1.2 ... 1.0 [0.2,1.9]
                                          80% 0.8 ... 0.8 [0.1,1.5]
Notes: All values converted to 2024 PPP. Calculations based on a social discount rate of 5%. ... 95% confidence intervals for program impacts in square brackets.
context_needed: Three RCTs of graduation programmes comparing group and individual coaching in Uganda, the Philippines and Bangladesh (Bangladesh also has a lighter individual arm). The programme effects themselves are in Table 1 (p. 21): ITT effects on the index of primary outcomes, monthly consumption per adult equivalent, food security, well-being, assets and income, at year 3 (Uganda, Philippines) and year 6 (Bangladesh), in 2024 PPP. Table 2 takes the consumption effect from Table 1, rounds it to whole dollars (Uganda individual $27 = 27.061; Bangladesh light $10 = 9.588), scales it to annual household consumption and projects it under persistence assumptions to compare with costs.

rule: Costs, projected benefits under persistence assumptions and benefit-cost ratios are never stored. Rows that repeat or rescale an effect reported in another table are stored again, labelled, and linked to that table with linked_to.

resolved_questions.question: Panel B 'Monthly consumption per adult equiv' repeats the Table 1 consumption ITT effects rounded to whole dollars, and 'Annual total household consumption' rescales the same effects to annual household totals with their own 95% CIs. Is a rescaled copy of an effect that is already stored from another table ever stored (for example as a second unit of the same effect), or always left out as a duplicate? This entry leaves both rows out.
resolved_questions.resolution: Decided by Lucas, 22 Nov 2026: store the repeated and rescaled effects in both places, linked.
